title: Smooth ascent of punctual purity over a trait
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a Noetherian local domain of dimension one and principal maximal ideal; a uniformizer $\pi$ generates that maximal ideal. Suppose $\ell$ is invertible on $S$. Let $X$ be a regular scheme of finite type over $S$, and let $q:Y\to X$ be a smooth finite-type morphism with $Y$ Noetherian [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. If $X$ is punctually pure, then $Y$ is regular and punctually pure.

source.place: Expose XVI Corollary 3.5.6, printed p.249; smooth input follows the diagonal/DNC lecture-notes route.

proof.text: Work on compatible affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$, $H=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $C\to B$ is smooth. The ring $C$ is regular, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] makes $B$ regular. These opens cover $Y$, proving its regularity. Fix $y\in U$, write $x=q(y)$ and $R=C_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Put $V=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_C R)$, $k=\kappa(x)$, $F=V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $v\in V$ be the point induced by $y$. The localization formula [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] identifies $\mathcal O_{V,v}=B_{\mathfrak q}=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. Thus punctual purity at $v$ is the desired assertion at $y$.

source.place: Corollary 3.5.6, p.249; local affine reduction, reconstructed using Stacks 07NF and the localization formula

proof.text: The maps $V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Their rings are regular and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] (a field is a regular ring). By [def-weil-regular-scheme], $R$ is regular local; choose generators $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of its maximal ideal, where $d=\dim R$. They form a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. Hence $i:\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R$ is regular of codimension $d$. Its pullback $i':F\hookrightarrow V$ has the same regular equations: smoothness gives flatness [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and tensoring each injective multiplication-by-$t_j$ map on $R/(t_1,\ldots,t_{j-1})$ with the flat $R$-algebra of $V$ preserves injectivity by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. At points of $F$ the final quotient is nonzero. Thus $i'$ is regular of codimension $d$ as well, including $d=0$.

source.place: Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2 and Proposition 3.2.3, p.244; flat pullback of the local regular pair

proof.text: Write $h:V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $h_F:F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $j$, $j'$ be the open complements of $i$, $i'$. Apply $h^*$ to the closed-support triangle $i_*i^!A_R\to A_R\to Rj_*A\to$ of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]; it stays distinguished [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Compare it with the triangle $i'_*i'^!A_V\to A_V\to Rj'_*A\to$ on $V$ by $b=1_{A_V}$ and $c=\operatorname{BC}:h^*Rj_*A\to Rj'_*A$ [sbc-def-base-change-map], an isomorphism by [sbc-thm-bounded-derived-smooth-base-change] (constant degree-zero $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf, $\ell$ invertible, $j$ qcqs as $R$ is Noetherian). Since BC is the unit of $j$ followed by the counit of $h$, the triangle identities give $c\circ h^*(\eta_j)=\eta_{j'}$. Closed direct image commutes with $h^*$: at points of $F$ both stalks of $h^*i_*M\to i'_*h_F^*M$ are $M$'s [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar], off $F$ both vanish [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar], so it is invertible [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Let $\beta:h_F^*i^!A_R\to i'^!A_V$ be the transpose of $i'_*h_F^*i^!A_R\simeq h^*i_*i^!A_R\to A_V$ and $a=i'_*\beta$. Rotating (TR2) and applying TR3 [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives $a'$ with $(a',b,c)$ a morphism of triangles. Both $a$ and $a'$ composed with the counit $i'_*i'^!A_V\to A_V$ give $h^*$ of the counit; as $\operatorname{Hom}(i'_*M,Rj'_*A[-1])=\operatorname{Hom}(j'^*i'_*M,A[-1])=0$ [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar], the target triangle forces $a=a'$. Now [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $a$ invertible, and the closed stalk formula detects this before $i'_*$: $\beta:h_F^*i^!A_R\simeq i'^!A_V$. No regular-base-change or arbitrary-field duality theorem is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.3, p.244, closed-support argument; smooth base change as used in Proposition 3.5.2, p.248, expanded via the localization triangles

proof.text: Punctual purity of $X$ at $x$ says exactly that $a_i:A_k\to i^!A_R(d)[2d]$ is an isomorphism. Pull it back by $h_F^*$. The flat-base-change compatibility, twist comparison and Kummer normalization of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] identify the resulting map, using the support exchange just proved, with $a_{i'}:A_F\to i'^!A_V(d)[2d]$. Consequently the regular pair $(V,F)$ is pure. No smooth orientation or trace theorem enters this identification: it is the flat-base-change clause of the supported Kummer class itself.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, p.248, pullback of a pure pair by smooth base change; class compatibility XVI 2.2.3.1 and 2.3.2

proof.text: Every local ring $\mathcal O_{F,z}$ is regular Noetherian, contains the prime field of $k$, and has $\ell$ invertible. Apply [lem-per-trait-test-prime-field-local-input] to this ring, for each $z\in F$. It gives exactly its canonical closed-point Kummer isomorphism, so $F$ is punctually pure. Apply [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three] to $i':F\hookrightarrow V$: condition (a) was proved in Step 4 and (b) is the preceding assertion, hence (c) gives punctual purity of $V$ at every point of $F$, including $v$. The local-ring identification in Step 1 identifies the closed-point immersions, dimensions and Kummer maps at $v$ and $y$, so $Y$ is punctually pure at $y$. Since $y$ was arbitrary the proof is complete; if $Y$ is empty the assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Propositions 3.2.3 and 3.2.5, pp.244--245, applied to the closed fibre; Corollary 3.5.6, p.249

Source read: ILO XVI §3.2–3.5 from the PDF, i.e. Prop 3.2.3 (two-of-three, p.244), Prop 3.2.5 (prime-field schemes are punctually pure, p.245), Prop 3.5.2 (local argument via smooth base change) and Cor 3.5.6 (p.249). The statement is the preserved one, as the Q91 repair note requires. It is 3.5.6 plus the explicit claim that Y is regular, and it adds finite type for q and Noetherian Y. The source's own proof goes through the global Gysin map Cl_{X/S} of 3.5.5, which needs an ample sheaf and the excluded trace formalism. The delivery instead runs the local 3.5.2 argument at x=q(y), and it is complete. Step 1: B_q is O_{V,v}=O_{Y,y}. Step 2: t_1..t_d stays a regular sequence on the flat V, so i':F→V is regular of codimension d. Step 3: smooth base change gives h_F^*i^!A≅i'^!A. Step 4: the class calculus's flat base change clause gives (a) for (V,F). Step 5: the prime-field local input on O_{F,z} gives (b), and two-of-three then gives purity at v, hence at y. Cases checked: Y empty, d=0, étale q, y not closed in its fibre, mixed characteristic, imperfect κ(x). FIX (E5, Step 3): the step called the three maps a morphism of triangles without checking compatibility with the connecting maps. The new text fills this in with TR2/TR3 [def-weil-triangulated-category] and BC∘h^*η_j=η_{j'} [sbc-def-base-change-map]. It then shows the fill-in equals the canonical i'_*β, because Hom(i'_*M,Rj'_*A[-1])=0 by lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar. Those two existing nodes were added to the step's uses and to proof_deps; no other field changed. No new nodes; no SGA; no cited dep is in route-pivot-dropped. Batch-5 flags are both outside the assumptions: lem-trf-regular-complete-coefficient-coordinates is the Cohen structure theorem (commutative algebra), and def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra is a general Sym/Proj definition.
